excerpt: Key improvements include new capability thresholds to indicate when we should upgrade our safeguards, refined processes for evaluating model capabilities and the adequacy of our safeguards (inspired by safety case methodologies), and new measures for internal governance and external input.
paraphrase: Key improvements include new capability thresholds, refined evaluation processes inspired by safety cases, and new internal governance and external input measures.

excerpt: We describe the most notable changes below.
paraphrase: The following entries describe the most notable changes.

excerpt: ASL definition changed: The term "ASL" now refers to groups of technical and operational safeguards (it previously also referred to models). We also introduced the new concepts of Capability Thresholds and Required Safeguards.
paraphrase: The ASL term now refers only to safeguard groups rather than models, and new concepts of Capability Thresholds and Required Safeguards were introduced.
prior_counterpart_excerpt: Note: We intend "ASL-N" to primarily refer to a specific set of safety measures that we might implement, similar to how BSL-N is a specification of safety measures required to meet a certain standard.

excerpt: This change allows for more targeted application of safeguards based on specific capabilities, rather than broad model categories.
paraphrase: The redefinition enables safeguards to be targeted at specific capabilities instead of broad model categories.

locator: Changelog / ARA threshold now a checkpoint
excerpt: ARA threshold now a checkpoint: We replaced our previous autonomous replication and adaption (ARA) threshold with a "checkpoint" for autonomous AI capabilities.
paraphrase: The former ARA threshold was replaced with a checkpoint concept for autonomous AI capabilities.
prior_locator: ASL-3 Capabilities and Threat Models / item 2
prior_counterpart_excerpt: Autonomous replication in the lab: The model shows early signs of autonomous self-replication ability, as defined by 50% aggregate success rate on the tasks listed in [Appendix on Autonomy Evaluations].

locator: Changelog / ARA threshold now a checkpoint
excerpt: Rather than triggering higher safety standards automatically, reaching this checkpoint will prompt additional evaluation of the model's capabilities and accelerate our preparation of stronger safeguards.
paraphrase: Reaching the checkpoint now triggers additional evaluation and accelerated safeguard preparation rather than automatic escalation.

locator: Changelog / ARA threshold now a checkpoint
excerpt: We previously considered these capabilities as a trigger for increased safeguards, motivated by an attempt to establish some threshold while we developed a better sense of potential threats.
paraphrase: Previously these capabilities triggered increased safeguards as a provisional threshold pending better threat understanding.
prior_locator: ASL-3 Capabilities and Threat Models / item 2
prior_counterpart_excerpt: Autonomous replication in the lab: The model shows early signs of autonomous self-replication ability, as defined by 50% aggregate success rate on the tasks listed in [Appendix on Autonomy Evaluations].

locator: Changelog / ARA threshold now a checkpoint
excerpt: We now believe that these capabilities - at the levels we initially considered - would not necessitate the ASL-3 standard.
paraphrase: Anthropic now believes these capability levels do not require the ASL-3 standard.

excerpt: AI R&D threshold added: We added a new threshold for AI systems that can significantly advance AI development.
paraphrase: A new threshold was added for AI systems capable of significantly advancing AI development.

excerpt: Such capabilities could lead to rapid, unpredictable advances in AI, potentially outpacing our ability to evaluate and address emerging risks, and may also serve as an early warning sign for the ability to automate R&D in other domains.
paraphrase: These capabilities could drive rapid unpredictable advances outpacing risk evaluation, and may signal broader R&D automation ability.

excerpt: Testing for Capability Thresholds: Rather than using prespecified evaluations, we now require an affirmative case that models are sufficiently far from Capability Thresholds.
paraphrase: Testing now requires an affirmative case of distance from Capability Thresholds rather than reliance on prespecified evaluations.
prior_counterpart_excerpt: Model evaluations: Evaluations are tests that are designed to detect dangerous capabilities. They should be conservative "warning signs" so as to avoid accidentally overshooting a critical safety threshold.

excerpt: Predefined tests may miss emerging risks or be overly conservative relative to the actual threshold of concern.
paraphrase: Predefined tests risk missing emerging threats or being overly conservative relative to the true threshold.

excerpt: Our most accurate tests change frequently enough that it is more practical to use this new approach than to have our Board of Directors pre-approve evaluations.
paraphrase: Because accurate tests change often, the affirmative-case approach is more practical than requiring Board pre-approval of evaluations.

excerpt: Adjusted evaluation cadence: We adjusted the comprehensive assessment cadence to 4x Effective Compute or six months of accumulated post-training enhancements (this was previously three months).
paraphrase: The comprehensive assessment cadence changed to 4x Effective Compute or six months of post-training enhancements, up from a prior three-month cadence.
stated_bar: 4x Effective Compute or six months (previously three months)
prior_counterpart_excerpt: Timing: During model training and fine-tuning, Anthropic will conduct an evaluation of its models for next-ASL capabilities both (1) after every 4x jump in effective compute, including if this occurs mid-training, and (2) every 3 months to monitor fine-tuning/tooling/etc improvements.
prior_stated_bar: every 4x jump in effective compute; every 3 months

excerpt: We found that a three-month cadence forced teams to prioritize conducting frequent evaluations over more comprehensive testing and improving methodologies.
paraphrase: The prior three-month cadence forced teams to prioritize frequent evaluation over comprehensive testing and methodology improvement.
